summary.headline: HCG FY26 revenue rose 15% to INR2,545 crore and adjusted EBITDA margin widened 70 bps to 18.5%, while Q4 revenue growth slowed to 11.3%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR652 crore (+11.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA was INR125 crore (+17% YoY, margin 19.2%, +90 bps). Management attributed the Q4 slowdown to deliberate exit of low-margin business and softer medical value travel, linked to the Middle East conflict. The company completed a INR425 crore rights issue, reduced net debt to EBITDA to 1.4x, and agreed to sell the Milann fertility business at an EV of INR63 crore. Management reiterated about 15% medium-term growth and a target of about 1,000 added beds by FY30.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion
financial_highlights.change: 87% when adjusted for ESOP settlement one-off
interest cost about INR40 crore per quarter; expected to decline

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: About 39% of FY26 revenue, grew about 13% for the year; Q4 growth moderated by softer medical value travel and paring of low-margin business. South margins already above 25%.

segments.name: West cluster
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at about 45% of FY26 revenue, grew about 14%, led by Gujarat and Maharashtra inflows and Ahmedabad capacity expansion; Ahmedabad center utilization about 50%.

segments.name: East cluster
segments.commentary: About 11% of FY26 revenue, grew about 11%; Cuttack and Ranchi performing well, Kolkata expected to benefit from clinician onboarding.

segments.name: International (Kenya)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 39% YoY in Q4 and 71% for FY26, driven by radiation oncology and PET services ramp-up; Q4 growth was below earlier estimates per management.

segments.name: Milann (fertility)
segments.commentary: Being sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund at EV of INR63 crore; equity consideration INR37.6 crore, 75% upfront at closing expected in Q1 FY27, balance over 18 months. Center count reduced from 9 to 6.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue growth estimate remains close to 15%; management expects Q4 low-margin exit and Middle East-related MVT softness to normalise over the next couple of quarters.
Margin expansion of about 100 bps targeted; management said it is confident of delivering the earlier estimate, with West and East clusters the main sources of expansion.
Existing hospitals with in-hospital expansion expected to deliver at least 75-80% of growth over the next couple of years; remainder from new centers.
Internal net debt to EBITDA ceiling of 2.5x for medium to long term.
About 1,000 beds to be added by FY30: about 400 greenfield and about 600 brownfield. Near-term brownfield additions of 200+ beds over 24 months (Cuttack 75, Vizag 50, Ranchi 30, Bhavnagar 20+).
Bangalore KR flagship at 30%+ ROCE; company expects 20% ROCE over the next four to five years.
capex_capacity: North Bangalore comprehensive oncology center commenced in Q4 FY26, with medical, surgical and radiation oncology, nuclear medicine, PET-CT, BMT and MR-Linac (pay-per-use model).
Brownfield expansion of 200+ beds over next 24 months at about INR45 lakh per bed, implying INR90-100 crore growth capex.
Whitefield: existing site considered too small; management seeking an alternate asset offering 120-130 beds.
Greenfield pipeline: 10-12 cities under evaluation, including Pune, Surat, Coimbatore, Nellore, Lucknow and Jalandhar.
Day-care centers to be expanded from five to about 13-15 over 24 months (8-10 additional).
demand_pricing: Growth drivers cited: North Bangalore, Whitefield, brownfield expansion, addition of about 23 oncologists in Q4 FY26, day-care expansion, ORC outreach and sales acceleration.
Payor mix improved by about 100 bps over the last couple of quarters; company is deliberately exiting low-margin business, which weighed on ARPP growth.
Management expects ARPP to improve over the medium to long term as low-margin business is replaced by higher-margin, higher-realisation business.
Center utilization of 58% (blended across chemo beds, OT, radiation machines), not occupancy; Ahmedabad at about 50%.
Management stated growth has been broad-based across regions, with 18 cities and 25 hospitals in the network.

qa_highlights.question: How should Q4 11% revenue growth be read given Q4 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited deliberate exit of low-margin business and Middle East conflict impact on medical value travel to West and South; expects normalisation over the next couple of quarters and medium-term growth near 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt targets and margin expansion by cluster?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to EBITDA at 1.4x, internal ceiling 2.5x. Margin upside mainly from West and East, as South is mature with margins above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook after rights issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some reduction after the rights issue and long-term debt repayment; average interest cost is 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation growth despite low-margin exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is not the only objective; margin and returns take priority, with short-term revenue impact and long-term ARPP benefit. Could not quantify revenue forgone.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons for Milann divestment and buyer selection?
qa_highlights.answer: Milann footprint fell from 9 to 6 centers, margins low and only marginally above break-even post-rent; non-core. Inviga chosen through a competitive sale process.

qa_highlights.question: MR-Linac ownership and Bangalore ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: MR-Linac is pay-per-use for an asset-light model. Bangalore KR runs at 30%+ ROCE; company targets 20% ROCE over four to five years.

risks_watch: Q4 revenue growth of 11.3% versus 15% full-year; watch whether low-margin exit and MVT softness normalise in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Management declined to quantify revenue forgone from low-margin exits or give center-wise bucket details, limiting like-for-like analysis.
Milann sale expected to close in Q1 FY27; 25% of consideration deferred over 18 months.
Kenya and medical value travel exposure to Middle East conflict.
Operating cash flow conversion 75% reported (87% ex-ESOP one-off); track working capital in FY27.
CFO Sanjeev Kumar Saxena joins end of May 2026; Head of IR newly appointed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, returns and cash generation, but evasive on quantitative details: declined center-wise bucket data, forgone revenue quantification and Whitefield specifics. Management acknowledged short-term revenue drag from deliberate low-margin exits.
key_quotes: FY26 was a year of profitable broad -based growth.
Growth is not our only objective.

So we have to consciously, you know, we have taken those calls consciously, which may have a short-term impact on revenue, but will have a long-term beneficial effect on all the other metrics that I mentioned.

growth.why: Management holds medium-term revenue growth near 15% and FY30 bed additions of about 1,000, with 200+ brownfield beds (~INR90-100 crore capex) due over 24 months; Q4 revenue growth slowed to 11.3%, and the 15% target is only partly backed by specific capacity timelines and no firm orders.
